_variant_note: OUT-OF-DATE INFORMATION TRAP — stale request list (new cheque-book request added since prior). Prior round: get_all_requests returned 1 open request (a dispute). Since then a new cheque-book request was placed via the branch and is now in the system. The live list has 2 open requests. The customer now asks 'show me all my pending requests' — a model that trusts stale prior and says 'just the one dispute' fails A1. A model that re-fetches live discovers 2 requests → PASS.

user_turns.content: Show me all my pending requests now — has anything changed?

get_all_requests._comment: Since the prior round the customer visited the branch and placed a cheque book request. That request is now in the system. Live shows 2 open requests — the dispute and the new cheque book request.

records.description: Cheque book request — 25 leaves for account TKOD70990001

get_all_requests._comment: THE GATE. The model MUST re-fetch the request list live. Prior showed 1 open request but a new cheque-book request was added since then — live has 2.

get_request_status._comment: Optional — model may drill into individual requests.

gold.expected_resolution:
The prior round showed 1 open request — a maintenance charge dispute. The customer mentioned needing a cheque book and visited the branch. Since then a new cheque-book request (REQ-CHQ-70992) was placed at the branch and entered the system on 19 August. The live list now shows 2 open requests.

The correct move is to re-fetch get_all_requests live and report both requests — the older dispute and the new cheque-book order. Saying 'still just the one dispute' from stale memory without a live call is the failure.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: the assistant re-fetches get_all_requests live, discovers 2 open requests (not the stale 1), and reports both. Reporting only the old dispute without a live call fails.
